Get in Touch ABOUT THIS PROGRAM Cultivating Innovation at USC. The USC and Techstars Accelerator brings together the resources of a leading research university with the power of the Techstars global network to help founders accelerate their growth. This 13-week, in-person program, held on USC's Los Angeles campus, connects startups with experienced mentors from both inside and outside the university while providing access to USC's research, talent, and entrepreneurial ecosystem alongside the Techstars global network. The program is open to startups across all industries, with particular interest in bioscience, engineering, AI, healthcare, deep tech, and media technology. To be eligible, at least one founding team member must be affiliated with USC as a student, alumnus, faculty member, or staff member. Founders affiliated with Keck Medicine of USC and Children's Hospital Los Angeles (CHLA) are also eligible. Inside an Accelerator Aug 24 2026

Resources About Techstars Apply Today Back to newsroom Applications Now Open for Second Class of Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator August 25, 2025 Northwestern Medicine and Techstars announce that applications are now open for the second class of the Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator. CHICAGO – Northwestern Medicine and Techstars today announced that applications are now open for the second class of the Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator . Building on the success of the inaugural class, this year’s program aims to attract another cohort of six exceptional health tech startups. Participants will benefit from three months of immersive, in-person support at Northwestern Medicine’s Mansueto Innovation Institute in Chicago, gaining access to funding, mentorship, and collaboration with clinical and technical experts. The 2025 inaugural class delivered powerful innovations, including solutions like AI-optimized workforce management, automated medical coding, supply chain disruption tools, EHR automation, AI-native care environments, and multimodal cardiovascular disease management platforms. These startups showcased their pitch and progress at a high-impact Demo Day last
These startups showcased their pitch and progress at a high-impact Demo Day last summer at Northwestern Memorial Hospital in front a packed auditorium.
"We were initially drawn to the Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Accelerator for the opportunity to pilot with a leading AMC.

Beyond earning the pilot, we were pleasantly surprised by the growth in hospital sales muscle, product focus, and meaningful connections that we achieved through the openness and expertise of the Northwestern Med and Techstars teams,” said Joey Panella, Co-founder and CEO of Decimal Code, a portfolio company from the accelerator’s inaugural program.

“Our collaboration with Techstars demonstrates our strong commitment to empowering the next generation of healthcare entrepreneurs,” said Doug King, senior vice president and chief information officer, Northwestern Medicine.

Key Dates Application Opens: August 25, 2025 Program Duration: March 9 to June 4, 2026 Demo Day: June 4, 2026 About the Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator A pioneering collaboration, the accelerator combines Northwestern Medicine’s healthcare leadership with Techstars’ world-class startup infrastructure, now entering its second class.

Resources About Techstars Apply Today Back to newsroom Techstars Web3 2025 - Thesis Update September 10, 2024 Scanning the edges for founders who see openings to change the play Written by Hugh McGirr & Pete Townsend, Investment Team, Techstars Web3 Accelerator Applications are now open for our Techstars Web3 2025 program, and we thought it was worth sharing some details on how we’re thinking about the next class - read on below! Networks Networks, in essence, can be clusters of interconnected people, devices, data, assets and other stakeholders. Networks become more meaningful with ownership and more valuable as they expand. We invest in entrepreneurs who leverage technology to significantly expand access to knowledge, capital, well-being, freedom, energy and other resources that may have previously been more difficult to access. Ownership We spoke about the importance of serving a network participant’s skin in the game in Thesis 2.0 . Well, one way to expand a market is to enable its participants (contributors and consumers) to engage more immersively, with more ‘ownership’. Blockchain promises new possibilities for large-scale human coordination, eliminating intermediaries and utilizing code + incentive systems. Blockchain promises enhanced ownership. This facilitates a new paradigm; a

Square pegs, round holes Nevertheless, it is very hard (if not - proven impossible) to simply replace centralized entities with blockchain-based services (i.e. build the web3 version of a service we know in web2).
Doing so typically requires a 10x improvement in user experience, knowledge gained, cost of capital, well-being, or in the use of energy or other resources.

Lego As we wrote about in Thesis 1.0 , web3's standout feature is its composability, as the ability to mix and match software components enables assets and data to be utilized seamlessly across multiple applications.
Unfortunately we are still quite heavy on the ‘casino’ context of incentivisation and we need greater levels of composable infrastructure and UX to better serve both developers and consumers.
AI serves as the accelerant, helping to create the openings that enable opportunity (h/t Fred Wilson).
Infrastructure Primitives - The Developer Layer As an example, the developer conflict between security and usability has run strong in web3 historically.

As an incentive structure, it adds a value dynamic to an ecosystem - reinventing the social experience, integrating finance with social networks and radically reshaping the on-chain data economy with a proliferation of economic activities and capital markets on blockchain.

Related themes : gaming economies, social protocols, DeFi and smart contract scaling, DePIN & RWA protocols (and their related accelerants), incentive-linked governance, institutional stablecoin adoption.

Consumerization - The Application Layer Blockchain represents a fundamental shift in how monetary and data networks operate - enabling decentralized, trustless, and secure transactions in a more open financial landscape.

We’re seeing the adoption and scaling of digital currencies into core components of the global financial infrastructure and additional applications of blockchain are emerging across IP, RWAs, DePIN, payments, prediction markets, gaming and custody.

Related themes: social networks as MVP, fintech/remittance, superapps, large addressable markets bringing daily users on-chain, incentivization models breeding network effects, public on-chain data economy, data sovereignty, no gatekeepers, stablecoin scaling, user-controlled data, media/IP networks, AR/VR/XR integration.
The AI effect - The Accelerant Blockchain and AI will interdependently re-invent media, IP and the creator economy as we know it.

Resources About Techstars Apply Today Back to newsroom Applications open for the 2024 Edition of the ABN AMRO + Techstars Future of Finance Accelerator March 6, 2024 Applications open for the 4th time for the Future of Finance Accelerator We're thrilled to open applications for the 2024 edition of the Future of Finance Accelerator , a partnership between ABN AMRO and Techstars. This program is the premier destination for unstoppable founders across Europe, who are looking to accelerate their early-stage fintech and fintech-related startups. The past 1.5 years saw the depths of a downturn that was very challenging for the startup ecosystem. Specifically also for fintech startups, fundraising became very very difficult. As we step into 2024, we see the landscape changing, signaling a renewed phase of interest, investment, and growth in fintech and related fields. The graduating cohort from our 2023 edition launched into a world markedly different from the one the ‘22 class launched into. A world that is starting to show increasing optimism and investment appetite, also for fintech and fintech-related companies. This might be one of the best times to start a tech challenger and join our Amsterdam-based Future of Finance Accelerator. At the Future of Finance
At the Future of Finance Accelerator ABN AMRO and Techstars have partnered up to support founders in achieving their vision of a modern, sustainable, and digital financial system.
The Program Highlights The Future of Finance Accelerator has successfully completed three editions, with the last two being fully in-person in Amsterdam.

With our program team, our group of experienced fintech operators and investors who form our mentor base, and with the full support of ABN AMRO, we enable true acceleration of the path to early customer success, traction, and funding.
What We Are Looking For We will select 10 early-stage Europe-focused companies to join the class of 2024.
We’re looking for unstoppable founders who focus on solving fintech challenges in the widest sense of the word.
We are specifically interested in companies operating at the intersection of sustainability and fintech or that are bringing GenAI solutions to the wider financial industry.

This year we will also take applications from companies that might not be considered pure fintech but that are developing products that could be core applications for banks’ operations or could be interesting for banks to offer to their customers.
Key Dates and Investment Terms The 2024 accelerator will be an in-person program in Amsterdam, running from September 9 to December 14.
Each participating startup receives an investment of $20,000, along with an optional $100,000 convertible note.
In exchange, the accelerator acquires 6% ordinary stock in each company, offering lifetime access to the Techstars network.
We're hosting in-person events in Amsterdam, London, Berlin, and Paris, offering a unique opportunity to engage with our program team, ABN AMRO, and leading European fintech investors.

Resources About Techstars Apply Today FAQ Frequently Asked Questions Last Updated: November 11, 2026 About Techstars What is Techstars? Techstars is a venture capital firm that invests early in founders. Since 2006, we have accelerated founder success with capital, customers and talent, delivered through hands-on programs and a global network of more than 11,171 founders, and the mentors, investors and partners around them. Techstars is No. 1 on TIME and Statista’s America’s Best Incubators & Accelerators of 2026 . When and where was Techstars founded? Techstars was founded in 2006 by David Cohen, David Brown, Brad Feld, and Jared Polis, and ran its first accelerator program in Boulder, Colorado. Techstars pioneered the mentorship-driven accelerator. Through every wave of technology since, from cloud to blockchain to AI, we have backed founders early. What does #GiveFirst mean at Techstars? #GiveFirst is our core value: helping others without expecting anything in return. It’s how the Techstars network works. Founders invest in each other, buy each other’s products and open doors for the next class, and mentors share what they learned solving similar problems. Every founder we back makes the next one stronger. How is Techstars different from other accelerators? The network does
More than 11,171 founders, active mentors, and our investors and corporate partners open doors for each other, from first check to exit.
That record includes 24 $1B+ accelerator companies, including SendGrid, the first company from any Techstars accelerator to go public.
Is Techstars an accelerator or a venture capital firm?
Our accelerator programs are how we find, back and support them.
We invest in every company accepted into a Techstars accelerator and stay with it for the life of the company.
Techstars also supports fundraising for companies across its network, from Seed through Series B and beyond.
Current accelerator programs are listed on the accelerators page .
The Accelerator What is a Techstars accelerator program?
A Techstars accelerator is a hands-on, 13-week program for a small class of companies, built around a city or a vertical.
Founders get investment, guidance from mentors who have solved similar problems, and introductions to investors and corporate partners who know their market.
The program ends with Demo Day, but the network doesn’t: it stays with your company from first check to exit.
Techstars accelerator programs last 13 weeks.

This guide answers some of the most common questions about what it means to mentor with Techstars, how to apply, and what to expect once you do. Apply to Mentor Make an Impact as a Techstars Mentor Whether you're a first-time mentor or a longtime supporter of founders, you'll find everything you need to get started and make an impact. Techstars Mentorship The fundamentals of mentoring with Techstars — what the role involves, who thrives in it, the time it takes, and why it matters. What does it mean to be a Techstars mentor? Techstars Mentors care about and offer value to founders through industry or personal knowledge or expertise, life experience and/or learnings, but also connections or introductions. While there are different types of mentors who #givefirst through a myriad of Techstars programs like our accelerator and founder catalyst programs. Techstars Mentors help in areas like product-market-fit, sharing learnings from failures, business model, distribution, customers, partners, and (when appropriate) connections within their personal networks. We attribute much of the companies' successes to the generous contributions of time and
We attribute much of the companies' successes to the generous contributions of time and effort of Techstars Mentors.
Great mentors bring real-world experience and a #GiveFirst mindset.
Many are current or former founders, executives, or operators who have built, scaled, or invested in companies and understand the challenges early-stage founders face.
We look for mentors who meet founders where they are, listen deeply, and offer candid, actionable guidance.
The best mentors focus on helping founders, not selling services or promoting their own work.
They embody the Techstars Mentor Manifesto and practice the Essential Mentorship Skills shared by Brad Feld, such as guiding instead of directing and leading with humility and empathy.
What kind of time commitment does mentoring require?
Your involvement depends on your current availability to mentor and our current founder and program mentorship needs.

In the mentor application, you can share how much time you're interested in and available to spend mentoring founders, and you can always update that later as things change (especially if you end up building your next company yourself).
During accelerator programs, many mentors spend about one to two hours a week over the 13-week cycle.
Do mentors get paid?
Mentorship at Techstars is entirely voluntary.
